لَازِبٌ Adhering, or adhesive, or cohesive, clay or mud. (S.) ―
-b2- Being, or remaining, fixed, settled, firm, or constant. (S.) ―
-b3- صَارَ الشَّىْءُ ضَرْبَةَ لَازِبٍ The thing became fixed, settled, firm, or constant, (S, K,) and severe: (TA:) [or, a constant infliction:] or, indispensable, or necessary: i. e., the blow of a sword that sticks, or remains fixed, [in the wound]. (Aboo-Bekr, cited in the TA.) لازب is here the same as لازم: (K:) the latter is the original word; the م being changed into ب; and is also used in this phrase: (TA:) but لازب, in this in-
stance, is the more chaste. (S.) En-Nábighah says, “فَلَا تَحْسِبُونَ الخَيْرَ لَا شَرَّ بَعْدَهُ
وَلَا تَحْسِبُونَ الشَّرَّ ضَرْبَةَ لَازِبِ
” [Then think ye not that good shall have no evil after it, nor think ye that evil shall be a constant infliction]. (S.) Sgh says, of the conversion of رِوَاغَةٌ into رِيَاغَةٌ, or of و into ى because of kesreh before it, هٰذَا القَلْبُ لَيْسَ بِضَرْبٍ لَازِبٍ [This conversion is not a necessary sort.] (TA in art. روغ.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
